I have enough evidence to make the minimal fix. The root cause: in `get_class_members` (sphinx/ext/autodoc/importer.py), inherited members are created as `ObjectMember(unmangled, value)` without `class_=subject`. Later, `ClassDocumenter.get_object_members` filters with `m.class_ == self.object`, so inherited annotation-only attributes (which have no value in the subclass `__dict__`) get dropped. The warning originates in `CDomain._resolve_xref_inner`, which parses the xref target with `parse_xref_object()` (a nested-name parser that rejects keywords like `int`/`bool`) and warns on failure. The fix: when the target is a single C keyword (a builtin type), skip resolution silently instead of warning.

I have enough evidence to make a targeted fix. The root cause: `parse_xref_object` only accepts a nested name, so a builtin type like `int` fails with "Expected identifier in nested name, got keyword: int". The fix is to let the xref parser accept a fundamental type spec (which yields no name, so no reference is created and no warning is emitted).
